HFT Practice · Lesson 0038

+

The GUI, and the Three Ways to Run a Trading Method (like the 2-Candle)

+
Why this matters: "run the 2-candle strategy" means +three different things in this codebase depending on the engine you pick — and the +desktop GUI, which predates the strategies package, runs none of them. Knowing which +door leads where saves you from hunting the GUI for a button that doesn't exist.
+ +

1 · The mental model: one pattern, three engines

+

The pattern (bullish/bearish engulfing — a red candle whose body is +swallowed by the next green one, or vice versa) is defined exactly once, in +strategies/engulfing.py. Three engines can drive it:

+ + + + + +
EngineCommandBar frequencyExit logicPersists?
Intraday PaperEngineintraday-sim1m–60m barsStop-loss / take-profit / forced end-of-day closeCSV files per run
Arena backtestarena-run backtestDailyOne-bar hold, next closeVerdict in arena.db
Arena livearena-run liveDailyOne-bar hold, next closeOngoing ledger in arena.db
+

The GUI is a fourth thing entirely: a Tkinter front-end over the +GBM/mean-variance pipeline (train, walk-forward, news, universe, +execution, metrics). It was built before strategies/ existed and has no +engulfing/arena tabs.

+ +

2 · The GUI tour

+
uv run gui-hft     # Docker users: MPLBACKEND=Agg is already set in docker-compose.yml
+

gui_app.py — class App(tk.Tk), six ttk.Notebook tabs +Each tab is a form wrapped around one CLI's functionality, run on a background +thread so the window doesn't freeze:

+ + + + + + + + +
TabWrapsWhat you do there
Walkforwardwalkforward-simPick a .joblib bundle + tickers file + dates, optionally pre-download OHLCV, hit Run Walkforward
Train/Backtestpaper-backtestTrain the GBM and save the bundle (Run Backtest + Save Model)
Universe Builderuniverse-builderScrape S&P 500 / NASDAQ ticker lists into tickers/
Newsnews-fetch / news-featuresPull Alpha Vantage sentiment, engineer features (needs ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY)
Executionrh-execPredict + allocate + (dry-run) submit. The "Dry run (no orders)" checkbox defaults to CHECKED — unticking it is the GUI's real-money gate
Analyze Equityanalyze-equityPoint at any equity CSV, get Sharpe/CAGR/MaxDD
+

Rule of thumb: anything the GUI does, the CLI does too (the tabs call the same +functions) — but not the reverse. Strategies, the arena, stress tests, SHAP, and +drift checks are CLI-only today.

+ +

3 · Running the 2-candle, both ways

+

Intraday, with stops (the PaperEngine path)

+
uv run intraday-sim --tickers AAPL,MSFT --start 2026-06-20 \
+    --interval 5m --strategy engulfing \
+    --position_dollars 1000 --stop_loss_pct 0.005 --take_profit_pct 0.01
+# outputs equity.csv + trades.csv; --no_short to go long-only
+# intervals: 1m 5m 15m 30m 60m — yfinance only serves ~7 days of 1m bars
+

Mechanics (strategies/paper_engine.py): a signal on bar N enters at bar +N+1's open; each later bar checks stop-loss first (it wins ties with take-profit); +any open position force-closes on the day's last bar — never hold overnight.

+ +

Daily, in the arena (screen → live → compare)

+
uv run arena-run backtest --start 2023-01-01 --end 2025-01-01 \
+    --strategies engulfing            # or engulfing,technical,meanrev
+uv run arena-run live                 # daily tick; breaker + divergence watching
+uv run arena-run report
+

Same pattern code, adapted to daily bars by +strategies/candlestick_daily.py (last two daily candles). One behavioral +difference to expect: the regime gate keeps engulfing out of trending +markets — a reversal pattern is a mean-reversion bet, so on trending days it holds +by design (disable with --no_regime_gate to experiment).

+ +

4 · Often confused

+ + + + + + +
PairThe difference
GUI Execution tab vs rh-execSame engine — the tab is a form over the executor. Both default to dry-run; the checkbox and --no_dry_run are the same gate wearing two outfits.
intraday-sim engulfing vs arena engulfingIdentical pattern detector, different worlds: 5-minute bars with SL/TP/EOD exits vs daily bars with one-bar holds, costs, sizing, and watchdogs. Their results are NOT comparable to each other.
Train/Backtest tab vs Walkforward tabTrain/Backtest fits the model once on a single split (optimistic, produces the bundle); Walkforward replays history without ever training on the traded day (honest validation). Lesson 0037's rule: validate with the second.
"strategy" in intraday-sim --strategy vs arena --strategiesTwo separate registries: intraday_sim.STRATEGIES (intraday contract, engulfing only today) vs strategies/registry.py (daily contract: engulfing, technical, meanrev, gbm).
+ +

5 · Practice

+

Score: 0 / 0

+ +
+

Q1. You open the GUI looking for a "run engulfing strategy" button. Where is it?

+
    +
  • Walkforward tab, under strategy dropdown
    • +
  • Nowhere — the GUI doesn't drive rule strategies; use intraday-sim or arena-run
    • +
  • Execution tab, strategy picker
    • +
  • Universe Builder tab
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q2. In an intraday-sim run, a bar triggers BOTH the stop-loss and the take-profit. What happens?

+
    +
  • Take-profit wins — you get the gain
    • +
  • Stop-loss wins — the engine assumes the worse fill
    • +
  • The position rides until end of day
    • +
  • The two exits average out
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q3. Arena-run live shows engulfing holding on a day when you can SEE a textbook engulfing pattern on the chart. Most likely reason?

+
    +
  • The daily adapter uses a different pattern definition
    • +
  • That day's market regime was classified trending/high_vol, so the gate held it out
    • +
  • The circuit breaker paused it
    • +
  • Both candles were dojis
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q4. Why does --interval 1m only work for recent dates?

+
    +
  • PaperEngine can't process that many bars
    • +
  • yfinance only provides ~7 days of 1-minute history
    • +
  • A repo setting blocks intervals under 5m
    • +
  • Alpha Vantage rate limits
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q5. The GUI Execution tab's dry-run checkbox: what's its default, and what does unticking it mean?

+
    +
  • Unchecked by default; ticking it simulates
    • +
  • Checked by default; unticking sends REAL orders via Robinhood
    • +
  • It toggles whether predictions run at all
    • +
  • It switches between arena paper and live ledgers
    • +
+

+
+ +

6 · Check your understanding (scenarios)

+
Scenario A. You want to know whether the 2-candle works better with tighter stops. Which engine, which flags, and what do you compare? +

Intraday engine — stops only exist there. Two runs differing only in +--stop_loss_pct (e.g. 0.005 vs 0.003), same tickers/dates/interval, +distinct --out_csv names, then analyze-equity --equity_csv on each. +The arena can't answer this: its daily one-bar hold has no stop-loss concept.

+
Scenario B. Your friend wants to try the platform but is command-line-averse. What CAN you honestly give them via the GUI, and where's the line? +

The full GBM lifecycle: train a model (Train/Backtest), validate it (Walkforward), +build ticker lists, pull news, compute metrics, and even dry-run executions — all +point-and-click. The line: anything strategy-arena related (2-candle, technical, +meanrev, ensembles, breaker, reports) is CLI-only today. A GUI arena tab would be a +reasonable future issue.

+
Scenario C. intraday-sim's engulfing made money last week but the arena's engulfing is EXCLUDED. Contradiction? +

No — different games. Intraday: 5-minute bars, SL/TP risk control, flat overnight. +Arena: daily bars, one-bar holds, transaction costs, screened over years of history. +A pattern can have intraday edge and no daily edge (or vice versa). The two results +answer different questions and neither invalidates the other.

+ + +
+ + Investigate per the method in your instructions, then return the findings list.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

The GUI, and the Three Ways to Run a Trading Method (like the 2-Candle)

Why this matters: "run the 2-candle strategy" means three different things in this codebase depending on the engine you pick — and the desktop GUI, which predates the strategies package, runs none of them. Knowing which door leads where saves you from hunting the GUI for a button that doesn't exist.

1 · The mental model: one pattern, three engines

I've read both changed files in full.

**Analysis:**

`docs/learning/index.html` — Static content only. The diff changes a count (`9` → `10`) and adds one `<div class="row">` linking to the new lesson. Pure static HTML/CSS with no scripts, no forms, no external inputs. No sinks.

`docs/learning/lessons/0038-gui-and-running-strategies.html` — Static lesson page with a tiny inline quiz `<script>`. Reviewed all sinks:

- `shuffle()` uses `Math.random()` — quiz option ordering only, not a security-relevant randomness use.
- Reads `li.dataset.correct` / `li.dataset.why` from **statically authored HTML** — no attacker-controlled source.
- Writes results via `feedback.textContent = ...` and `document.getElementById('score').textContent = ...` — `textContent` is not an HTML-parsing sink; even if `data-why` contained markup, it can't inject.
- `feedback.style.color` is assigned one of two hard-coded CSS variable strings (`var(--good)` / `var(--bad)`) — no attacker input reaches CSS.
- No `innerHTML`, `document.write`, `eval`, `new Function`, `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `location.*` reads, `postMessage` listeners, URL/query-string parsing, cookie/storage access, or external `<script src=>`.
- No forms, no outbound links with `target="_blank"`, no OAuth/callback surfaces.
- Content is baked at generation time; there is no user-supplied data flowing anywhere.

There are no entry points, no attacker-influenceable data flows, no auth/policy logic, no credentials, and no dangerous sinks introduced. This is inert educational documentation.
